# TIGAS

Thin-Client Interactive Gaussian Adaptive Streaming over HTTP/3 (formerly
Gaussian Adaptive Streamer). Server-side 3D Gaussian Splatting renders a
scene and streams it to a browser client over HTTP/3 / WebTransport with
DASH-style ABR. This checkout is the **paper-validated** codebase (fork of
[Rekenar/GaussianAdaptiveStreamer](https://github.com/Rekenar/GaussianAdaptiveStreamer));
co-author experiment paths live here.

The companion ACM paper lives in
[68c9198c30495c4e43526835/](68c9198c30495c4e43526835/) — a separate git repo
(Overleaf sync, gitignored here) with its own history. Don't apply this
file's rules there.

An unfinished modular redesign (contract-first `src/tigas/`, headless eval,
ABR profiles) is preserved only on branch `archive/modular-scaffold` (and
tag `archive/tigas-native-stack` for the pre-pivot native/Go tree). Do
**not** treat that branch as `main` or mix its layout into this tree without
an explicit fusion plan.

**`AGENTS.md` is the only rule file to edit by hand.** Cursor, Antigravity,
Codex and Copilot's cloud agent read it natively and in full. Claude Code has
no AGENTS.md support, so `CLAUDE.md` imports a generated slice instead. The
`host-rules` block at the end, `.cursor/rules/cursor-harness.mdc`,
`.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.claude/project-core.md`, `.claude/rules/`
and `.github/instructions/` are all generated by `tools/sync_agent_rules.py`
— edit `AGENTS.md` outside the host block,
then re-run `python3 tools/sync_agent_rules.py` before committing (this repo
has no pre-commit/CI gate for it yet).

A section marked `<!-- scope: <globs> -->` above its heading stays in this file

## Entry points

Everything runs inside the `render` conda env, with deps from
`requirements.txt` (PyTorch cu118 / gsplat stack — see `readme.md`):

```
cd /home/itec/emanuele/TIGAS
conda activate render
./run.sh
# equivalent:
python http3_server.py \
  --certificate certificates/ssl_cert.pem \
  --private-key certificates/ssl_key.pem \
  --host 0.0.0.0
```

Chrome needs QUIC/WebTransport flags (Linux/macOS snippets in `readme.md`).
Place PLY models under `static/models/<modelID>/` (gitignored content).

Key modules:

- `http3_server.py` — aioquic HTTP/3 + WebTransport process entry
- `gs_app.py` — Starlette ASGI app + `/wt` render loop
- `routes.py` — HTTP handlers (models UI, players, experiments, DASH, SR)
- `experiments.py` — experiment export/zip, predict logging, `tc` helpers
- `dash_streamer.py` — live ffmpeg → CMAF/DASH
- `render.py` / `models.py` — gsplat rasterization and model cache
- `templates/player_wt.html`, `player_dash.html`, `player.html` — clients
- `static/abrs/` — client ABR algorithms (`Throughput.js`, `L2A.js`, `LoL+.js`, …)

Experiment inputs (tracked):

- Network traces: `traces/*.csv` (LTE shaping + Ghent mobility traces)
- Camera/pose playback: `TestMovements/` (EyeNav train + Rutgers + NTHU)

Helpers:

- `scripts/bandwidth_fluctuations.sh` — `tc` shaping from a trace CSV
- `scripts/run_all_metrics.sh` / `scripts/compute_metrics.py` — offline
  PSNR/SSIM/VMAF over exported frame folders
- `scripts/convert_eyenav_csv.py` / `scripts/csv_data_converter/` — pose
  trace conversion
- `reset_interface.sh` — network/tc reset

## `experiment/` / `captures/` — deletion is unrecoverable

`experiment/` and `captures/` are gitignored and hold session artifacts that
cost real interactive GPU time to reproduce; none of it is in git history. A
`~/.agent-rules/scripts/guard-rm.py` PreToolUse hook (configured in this
repo's `.claude/settings.json`) blocks `rm` against those whole trees;
deleting one specific `experiment/<run>/` or `captures/<…>/` subdirectory
stays allowed. Tracked assets (`traces/`, `TestMovements/`, `certificates/`)
are a `git checkout` away and do not need the same protection.

## Concurrent sessions & git hygiene

This checkout is shared across multiple agent sessions. A branch alone does
not isolate a session; two agents sharing one working directory share one
HEAD. For any substantive change, work in a dedicated worktree + branch
(`git worktree add ../wt-tigas/<slug> -b <type>/<slug>`) rather than editing
directly in the main checkout. Before deleting any branch, read it first
(`git log main..<branch>`) and tag-and-push (`git tag archive/<branch>`) if
it holds work `main` doesn't have — see the host-wide git rules below.
Preserve remote branches such as `mac-os` and `archive/modular-scaffold`
unless deliberately retired after reading them.

## The paper is the primary living document

The manuscript (`68c9198c30495c4e43526835/main.tex` + figures/bib) is the
living research document. Prefer folding findings into the paper with the
`/update-paper` skill once results are committed and trustworthy. If the
paper repo later adopts `STATUS/GOAL/HOLE/NOTE/NEXT/CLAIM` markers and a
`RESEARCH_LOG.md` (sibling projects already do), grep those before planning
experiments so we only run what the paper needs.

## Rules that load on demand

These sections of `AGENTS.md` are not in this file. They arrive automatically the moment you read a file they cover, so you do not need to fetch them by hand — but if you are reasoning about one of these areas *without* opening its files, read the matching file under `.claude/rules/` first.
